short: The first major campaign fought entirely by air forces, over southern England in 1940.
full:
Following the fall of France, Germany needed air superiority over the Channel before any seaborne invasion of Britain could be attempted. From July to October 1940 the Luftwaffe attacked shipping, airfields, radar stations and ultimately cities.

RAF Fighter Command's advantage was not aircraft quality but system: the Dowding System integrated radar, the Observer Corps and telephone plotting rooms into the world's first ground-controlled interception network, letting outnumbered squadrons be sent where they mattered. The German switch to bombing London in September relieved pressure on the airfields at a critical moment. Invasion was postponed indefinitely on 17 September, and the campaign became the first strategic defeat inflicted on Nazi Germany.
